newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to try boycott party militants - rights group.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to try boycott party militants - rights group.

text.p: Seven members of a Moroccan party are to be tried after campaigning for a boycott of local elections due on Friday, a spokeswoman for the independent Human Rights Association (AMDH) said on Wednesday.

The seven members of the opposition Avant-Garde Democratique et Socialiste party (PADS), "were arrested by police in Rabat and the northern city of Tangier while campaigning against the polls of June 13," an AMDH spokeswoman told Reuters.
They will appear before a Rabat court on Friday, the day of the election, she added.
Officials at the ministries of human rights and justice were not available for comment but one official who asked not to be named said activists had been arrested for disturbing public order.
In a statement sent to local media, the PADS said a total of 125 activists, including a woman were arrested in more than 26 provinces throughout the country recently for their boycott campaign.
"Some of our arrested members were sentenced to up to two months in jail while others are waiting similar sentences," it added.
Among Morocco's dozen active parties, the PADS was the only opposition group to call for the boycott of local elections.
